items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: a guy by the name of Bruce Scott started a magazine... It’s a listing. It’s a place where all the listings can appear...

ctx.x: Is there a live music scene where you live in Florida of any extent?

Yeah, it’s getting better too. I think the main reason is about a year ago, maybe a little over a year ago, a guy by the name of Bruce Scott started a magazine, like one of those small booklet-sized magazines, styled after the Hot House, in New York. It’s a listing. It’s a place where all the listings can appear, and the clubs, and record companies, and whoever else in the music business, whether it be artists or big companies, whatever, can advertise whatever it is. Advertise a concert, advertise a record,…

and fractured, but now, to somebody coming to that area, a tourist coming to that area can get this one book and see, this is happening in South Beach and this is happening in Ft. Lauderdale, and this is happening in Palm Beach County. And it’s sort of something like to keep track of the music scene as a whole, taking the music scene as a whole. Because in my opinion the problem with music is just like the same problem that we have politically and everything now with everything splitting off into — like cable TV…
